"'''It Must Have Been Love'''", originally "'''It Must Have Been Love (Christmas for the Broken Hearted)'''", is a song written by [[Per Gessle]] and performed by the Swedish pop duo [[Roxette]]. The [[power ballad]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/uk/go/44642|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180927180222/http://www.denofgeek.com/uk/go/44642|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 September 2018|title=24 of the Biggest and Best Movie Power Ballads|website=Denofgeeek.com|access-date=24 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://myq105.com/listicle/best-power-ballads/|title=50 Best Power Ballads of All Time|website=Q105|date=14 February 2024|access-date=11 June 2023|archive-date=11 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611010608/https://myq105.com/listicle/best-power-ballads/|url-status=dead}}</ref> became the duo's third number one hit in the United States,<ref name=USsingles>{{cite magazine|url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=roxette|chart=Hot 100}}|title=Roxette - Chart History on the Billboard Hot 100 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]  |access-date=19 November 2016}}</ref> and is one of their best selling releases, being certified gold or platinum in a number of countries. It remains their best-known and [[List of signature songs|signature song]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 June 2012 |title=Roxette unveil new song ahead of UK shows |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/music/a389834/roxette-unveil-new-track-ahead-of-uk-arena-shows-listen/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240611221908/https://www.digitalspy.com/music/a389834/roxette-unveil-new-track-ahead-of-uk-arena-shows-listen/ |archive-date=11 June 2024 |access-date= |website=Digital Spy |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Five different versions of the song have been officially released. The original song was released in 1987, which was followed by the most successful incarnation, a slightly edited and overdubbed version, omitting the Christmas references, created for the [[Pretty Woman (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] to the 1990 film ''[[Pretty Woman]]''. During the "Join the Joyride! World Tour" in 1991, the band recorded a [[country music]] version in [[Los Angeles]], included on their 1992 album ''[[Tourism (Roxette album)|Tourism]]''. A Spanish-language version of the ''Pretty Woman'' recording was released on their 1996 compilation ''[[Baladas en Español]]''. Finally, an orchestral live performance from the band's 2009 concert at [[Night of the Proms]] was included on their 2012 studio album, ''[[Travelling (Roxette album)|Travelling]]''.

"It Must Have Been Love", originally "It Must Have Been Love (Christmas for the Broken Hearted)", is a song written by Per Gessle and performed by the Swedish pop duo Roxette. The power ballad became the duo's third number one hit in the United States, and is one of their best selling releases, being certified gold or platinum in a number of countries. It remains their best-known and signature song.

Five different versions of the song have been officially released. The original song was released in 1987, which was followed by the most successful incarnation, a slightly edited and overdubbed version, omitting the Christmas references, created for the soundtrack to the 1990 film Pretty Woman. During the "Join the Joyride! World Tour" in 1991, the band recorded a country music version in Los Angeles, included on their 1992 album Tourism. A Spanish-language version of the Pretty Woman recording was released on their 1996 compilation Baladas en Español. Finally, an orchestral live performance from the band's 2009 concert at Night of the Proms was included on their 2012 studio album, Travelling.

During a run of increasingly successful singles from the duo's 1988 album Look Sharp!, Touchstone Pictures approached Roxette and their label about contributing a song to the soundtrack of the upcoming romantic comedy release Pretty Woman, starring Richard Gere and Julia Roberts. The film was released in March 1990 and went on to make more than US$460 million at the worldwide box office. The corresponding soundtrack album was also a commercial success, which was certified triple-platinum in the US. The soundtrack went on to sell more than nine million copies worldwide.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
Bill Coleman from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine described the song as a "rhythmic [[Sentimental ballad|ballad]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Bill|last=Coleman|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1990/BB-1990-03-31.pdf|title=Single Reviews|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=31 March 1990|access-date=14 February 2020|page=78}}</ref> Dave Sholin from the ''[[Gavin Report]]'' wrote: "[[Per Gessle|Per]] and [[Marie Fredriksson|Marie]] are on target again. Per Gessle continues to demonstrate his uncanny ability to compose exceptional pop melodies and Marie Fredriksson makes the words and music jump through the speakers. Though timed to coincide with the release of the [[Julia Roberts]]/[[Richard Gere]] film ''[[Pretty Woman]]'', this tune from the soundtrack could easily stand on its own. Interest in the movie only gives it that much more of a boost".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Dave |last= Sholin |title= Gavin Picks > Singles |magazine= [[Gavin Report]] |issue= 1799 |date= 23 March 1990 |page= 52 |access-date= 17 April 2018 |url= https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Gavin-Report/90/90/Gavin-1990-03-23.pdf}}</ref> Dave Simpson from ''[[The Guardian]]'' said the song is a "masterpiece of pain". He added that "Fredriksson's genius is in delivering the title line clean and stoic, rather than with tortured vibrato, to show that she's resigned to her fate. But with the jarringly urgent upward key change in the middle eight, the pain floods in again, and she's back to square one".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Dave|last=Simpson|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/dec/10/it-must-have-been-love-roxettes-power-ballad-is-a-masterpiece-of-pain|title=It Must Have Been Love: Roxette's power ballad is a masterpiece of pain|magazine=[[The Guardian]]|date=10 December 2019|access-date=7 March 2020}}</ref>

A reviewer from ''[[Liverpool Echo]]'' wrote: "It's a ballad, it's big in America, but it's not as heavy-handed as the usual US success. Funnily enough, there even seems to be a bit of an [[ABBA]] influence in there".<ref>"New singles". ''[[Liverpool Echo]]''. 21 May 1990. p. 17.</ref> [[Refinery29]] included it at number 39 on their list of ''The Saddest Breakup Songs of All Time'', saying the track "represents the perfect ratio of schlock to sentiment. In someone like [[Celine Dion]]'s hands, this would have been a complete disaster, but the Swedish duo gaze off to 'where the water flows' and 'where the wind blows' without sounding like '90s [[Walt Disney|Disney]] characters".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-ca/2019/11/8737469/the-saddest-breakup-songs-of-all-time#slide-34 |title=The Saddest Breakup Songs of All Time |work=[[Refinery29]] |date=8 November 2019 |access-date=9 December 2019}}</ref> Brendon Veevers from ''[[Renowned for Sound]]'' noted the song as a "timeless [[power ballad]] that has aged like a fine wine".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://renownedforsound.com/index.php/top-10-roxette-ballads/|last=Veevers|first=Brendon|title=TOP 10 ROXETTE BALLADS|website=[[Renowned for Sound]]|date=12 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315173311/http://renownedforsound.com/index.php/top-10-roxette-ballads/|access-date=21 April 2020|archive-date=15 March 2015}}</ref>

Though timed to coincide with the release of the Julia Roberts/Richard Gere film Pretty Woman, this tune from the soundtrack could easily stand on its own. Interest in the movie only gives it that much more of a boost". Dave Simpson from The Guardian said the song is a "masterpiece of pain". He added that "Fredriksson's genius is in delivering the title line clean and stoic, rather than with tortured vibrato, to show that she's resigned to her fate. But with the jarringly urgent upward key change in the middle eight, the pain floods in again, and she's back to square one".

A reviewer from Liverpool Echo wrote: "It's a ballad, it's big in America, but it's not as heavy-handed as the usual US success. Funnily enough, there even seems to be a bit of an ABBA influence in there". Refinery29 included it at number 39 on their list of The Saddest Breakup Songs of All Time, saying the track "represents the perfect ratio of schlock to sentiment. In someone like Celine Dion's hands, this would have been a complete disaster, but the Swedish duo gaze off to 'where the water flows' and 'where the wind blows' without sounding like '90s Disney characters". Brendon Veevers from Renowned for Sound noted the song as a "timeless power ballad that has aged like a fine wine".

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
A re-written and edited version of the track – the lyric "It's a hard Christmas day" was changed to "It's a hard winter's day" and 24 seconds were removed from the outro<ref name="MTV"/> – became an international hit during the summer of 1990. It was not the first single released from the ''Pretty Woman'' soundtrack, but it became the most successful, spending two weeks at the top spot of the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in June.<ref name="People"/> The song was certified Gold by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) for sales in excess of 500,000 copies in the US.<ref name="riaa"/> At the end of the year, ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' listed it as the second most successful single of 1990, behind [[Wilson Phillips]]' "[[Hold On (Wilson Phillips song)|Hold On]]".<ref name="US1990">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/yearend_chart_display.jsp?f=The+Billboard+Hot+100&g=Year-end+Singles&year=1990 |title=Billboard Year End Charts - Year End Singles - 1990 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]  |access-date=19 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070102110431/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/yearend_chart_display.jsp?f=The%2BBillboard%2BHot%2B100&g=Year-end%2BSingles&year=1990 |archive-date=2 January 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The single peaked at number three in the UK—their highest-peaking single there. It stayed on the [[UK Singles Chart]] for 14 weeks,<ref name="uk"/> and was certified gold by the [[British Phonographic Industry]] (BPI) for sales and streams in excess of 400,000.<ref name="bpi"/> The song was re-released in the UK and Ireland in September 1993 to tie in with the TV premiere of ''Pretty Woman'',<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thelookforroxette.com/releases.html?id=946 |title=It Must Have Been Love - the Look for Roxette.com (BETA): Worldwide Discography & Price Guide :: Releases |access-date=16 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116173628/https://www.thelookforroxette.com/releases.html?id=946 |archive-date=16 November 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> peaking at number ten in both countries.<ref name="uk"/><ref name="ireland"/> It became Roxette's second of three number one singles in Australia, spending two weeks at the top spot in July 1990.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.noise11.com/news/aria-singles-report-avicii-is-longest-number-one-swedish-act-since-roxette-20130803 |title=ARIA Singles Report: Avicii Is Longest Number One Swedish Act Since Roxette |first=Gavin |last=Ryan |work=[[Noise11]] |publisher=[[Paul Cashmere]] |date=3 August 2013 |access-date=14 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512215817/http://www.noise11.com/news/aria-singles-report-avicii-is-longest-number-one-swedish-act-since-roxette-20130803 |archive-date=12 May 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref> The song was a massive hit in Norway, where it spent twelve weeks at number one.<ref name="norway"/> In Switzerland, the song spent three non-consecutive weeks at number one.<ref name="switzerland"/> It also reached number one in Canada, Poland and Spain, and the top five in Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand and West Germany, where it spent nine months in the top 75.<ref name="germany"/>

In 2005, Gessle received an award from [[Broadcast Music Incorporated|BMI]] after the song's four millionth radio play in the US.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bmi.com/news/entry/534322 |title=2005 BMI awards |publisher=[[Broadcast Music Incorporated|BMI]] |date=28 November 2005 |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315222153/http://www.bmi.com/news/entry/534322 |archive-date=15 March 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> He received updated awards from the same organization after its five millionth radio play in 2014,<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/news/record-labels/6281704/nile-rodgers-ellie-goulding-honored-at-bmi-london-awards |title=Nile Rogers, Ellie Goulding Honored at BMI London Awards |first=Marc |last=Schneider |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]  |date=14 October 2014 |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100948/http://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/news/record-labels/6281704/nile-rodgers-ellie-goulding-honored-at-bmi-london-awards |archive-date=7 September 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref> and its six millionth play in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bmi.com/news/entry/bmi-2021-london-awards|title=BMI Celebrates its 2021 London Award Winners|work=BMI|date=11 October 2021|access-date=25 November 2021}}</ref>

As of May 2026, the song has over 1 billion streams on [[Spotify]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://open.spotify.com/track/6kvoHl80mfCVTv7XnZkjQn?si=7dfdb7a50a094d87|title=Spotify|website=Open.spotify.com|access-date=18 July 2026}}</ref>

A re-written and edited version of the track – the lyric "It's a hard Christmas day" was changed to "It's a hard winter's day" and 24 seconds were removed from the outro – became an international hit during the summer of 1990. It was not the first single released from the Pretty Woman soundtrack, but it became the most successful, spending two weeks at the top spot of the US Billboard Hot 100 in June. The song was certified Gold by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for sales in excess of 500,000 copies in the US. At the end of the year, Billboard listed it as the second most successful single of 1990, behind Wilson Phillips' "Hold On".

The single peaked at number three in the UK—their highest-peaking single there. It stayed on the UK Singles Chart for 14 weeks, and was certified gold by the British Phonographic Industry (BPI) for sales and streams in excess of 400,000. The song was re-released in the UK and Ireland in September 1993 to tie in with the TV premiere of Pretty Woman, peaking at number ten in both countries. It became Roxette's second of three number one singles in Australia, spending two weeks at the top spot in July 1990. The song was a massive hit in Norway, where it spent twelve weeks at number one. In Switzerland, the song spent three non-consecutive weeks at number one. It also reached number one in Canada, Poland and Spain, and the top five in Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand and West Germany, where it spent nine months in the top 75.

In 2005, Gessle received an award from BMI after the song's four millionth radio play in the US. He received updated awards from the same organization after its five millionth radio play in 2014, and its six millionth play in 2021.

As of May 2026, the song has over 1 billion streams on Spotify.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The second video was directed by Doug Freel and was shot in a warehouse. It included clips from ''Pretty Woman'', with Fredriksson singing and playing piano and Gessle playing guitar between various prop changes.<ref name="rox-dvd"/> There is also an alternate version of the video, without the movie scenes, which was available solely on the VHS ''[[The Videos (Roxette video)|The Videos]]''. According to Fredriksson, shooting this video was a surreal experience, as Freel "wanted all movements in slow motion, so I had to lip-sync the vocals at double speed. My first lesson in how to sing an emotional ballad Mickey Mouse style".<ref name="liner"/> 

As of June 2026, this video has more than 987 million views on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Roxette|title=Roxette - It Must Have Been Love|website=[[YouTube]] |date=4 March 2009|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k2C5TjS2sh4|access-date=11 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170624055843/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k2C5TjS2sh4|archive-date=24 June 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>
sections.text:
The second video was directed by Doug Freel and was shot in a warehouse. It included clips from Pretty Woman, with Fredriksson singing and playing piano and Gessle playing guitar between various prop changes. There is also an alternate version of the video, without the movie scenes, which was available solely on the VHS The Videos. According to Fredriksson, shooting this video was a surreal experience, as Freel "wanted all movements in slow motion, so I had to lip-sync the vocals at double speed. My first lesson in how to sing an emotional ballad Mickey Mouse style". 

As of June 2026, this video has more than 987 million views on YouTube.

sections.heading: 25th anniversary reissue (2015)
sections.wikitext: On the twenty-fifth anniversary of the song's release on the ''Pretty Woman'' soundtrack,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://roxette.se/discography.php?show=release&id=124 |title=Roxette - Discography |work=Roxette.se |access-date=20 November 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121042346/http://roxette.se/discography.php?show=release&id=124 |archive-date=21 November 2016}}</ref> [[Parlophone Records|Parlophone]] released a limited edition [[Unusual types of gramophone records#Colored records|red-coloured vinyl]] on 19 May 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.amazon.com/Must-Have-Been-Love-25th-Anniversary/dp/B00ULE2UXU |title=Roxette - It Must Have Been Love - 25th Anniversary |work=[[Amazon Music]] |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121043734/https://www.amazon.com/Must-Have-Been-Love-25th-Anniversary/dp/B00ULE2UXU |archive-date=21 November 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref> This single included the ''Pretty Woman'' version of the song, backed with the original 1987 release and the [[Los Angeles]]-studio performance (minus the live intro recorded in [[Santiago]], [[Chile]]) from their 1992 album ''[[Tourism (Roxette album)|Tourism]]''. The latter features [[pedal steel guitar]] performed by [[Greg Leisz]], who is best known for his work with [[k.d. lang]]. The single was released via [[Online music store|digital download]] stores on 23 March.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/it-must-have-been-love-single/976541442 |title=It Must Have Been Love - Single by Roxette on Apple Music |work=[[Apple Music]] |date=23 March 2015 |publisher=[[Apple Inc.|Apple]] |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121043107/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/it-must-have-been-love-single/id976541442 |archive-date=21 November 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref>
sections.text: On the twenty-fifth anniversary of the song's release on the Pretty Woman soundtrack, Parlophone released a limited edition red-coloured vinyl on 19 May 2015. This single included the Pretty Woman version of the song, backed with the original 1987 release and the Los Angeles-studio performance (minus the live intro recorded in Santiago, Chile) from their 1992 album Tourism. The latter features pedal steel guitar performed by Greg Leisz, who is best known for his work with k.d. lang. The single was released via digital download stores on 23 March.

sections.heading: Philly Lutaaya version
sections.wikitext: In 1989, the late Ugandan musician [[Philly Lutaaya]], who was then based in Sweden used the song to record his hit "Alone and Frightened" on his album "Alone", in which he came out as an HIV/AIDS patient, becoming the first public figure to be identified with the virus/disease during an HIV/AIDS epidemic in Uganda.<ref>{{cite web |title=First song by Ugandan superstar to address HIV/AIDS pandemic –Alone and Frightened by Philly Lutaaya |url=https://matookerepublic.com/2016/05/30/these-twelve-songs-hold-special-records-in-ugandan-music/ |website=Matooke Republic |date=30 May 2016 |access-date=18 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918160746/https://matookerepublic.com/2016/05/30/these-twelve-songs-hold-special-records-in-ugandan-music/ |archive-date=18 September 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Late Philly Bongoley Lutaaya Vs Roxette |url=https://www.newvision.co.ug/new_vision/news/1007416/late-philly-bongoley-lutaaya-vs-roxette |website=New Vision |access-date=18 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918160649/https://www.newvision.co.ug/new_vision/news/1007416/late-philly-bongoley-lutaaya-vs-roxette |archive-date=18 September 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>
